summary:
We developed PACHA SCAN, a web platform that transforms satellite data into visual and easy-to-understand information to monitor changes across Peruvian territories and contribute to the prevention of and response to environmental risks.

We believe this platform is particularly important because, in recent months, several areas of Peru have been affected by forest fires, posing a serious threat to ecosystems, wildlife, and local communities.

As we have witnessed, communities that have lost their crops and livestock have also lost the daily livelihoods that sustain their families. Therefore, accessible information is essential to help people monitor what is happening on their land and prevent crop destruction, soil degradation, and livestock losses.

Our goal is to empower Peruvians to protect their land and natural resources, visualize satellite detections, and understand the changes taking place in their surroundings so they can make better-informed decisions.

Furthermore, we aim to break educational barriers by bringing astronomy and space science closer to communities beyond Lima. Our project seeks to transform the way people interact with their environment by connecting the daily work of those who cultivate the land with the observation and study of our planet from space.
details:
PACHA SCAN transforms satellite data into accessible visual information through interactive maps, helping users monitor changes in Peruvian territories and identify potential environmental threats, including possible forest fires. By connecting space technology with local needs, the platform aims to support farmers in monitoring their land, protecting crops and livestock, and making better-informed agricultural decisions. Its innovation lies in bringing Earth observation technology closer to rural communities, combining environmental protection, agricultural awareness, and space science education. Developed with Peru's environmental challenges, geographical diversity, and community needs in mind, our project seeks to strengthen prevention, promote scientific knowledge, and contribute to a safer and more sustainable future.

PACHA SCAN was developed as a modular Single Page Application (SPA) using JavaScript (ES6+), JSX, HTML5, CSS3, SVG, and JSON. It uses React 18 and Vite 5, with a component-based architecture organized into orchestration, UI components, data management, and utilities. We also integrated Leaflet for interactive maps, Chart.js for data visualization, and Lucide React for interface icons. The project incorporates satellite observation data sources such as NASA NISAR and NASA FIRMS.
